pages.title: Security and authentication | Zendesk Developer Docs
pages.text: Security and authentication | Zendesk Developer Docs Documentation API Reference Search / Introduction Home Introduction Introduction Developer community Document conventions Examples Plan availability Security and authentication Rate limits Requests Data types Pagination Working with AI tools Change policy Undocumented APIs On this page OAuth access token Global OAuth access token API token (deprecated) SSL requirements End user authentication Security and authentication On this page OAuth access token Global OAuth access token API token (deprecated) SSL requirements End user authentication Copy page You must be a verified user to make API requests. Zendesk supports using OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests. Note: If you're an existing Zendesk customer and are currently using basic authentication or API tokens, you will have to migrate to OAuth access tokens for improved security and compatibility with future requirements. If you plan on distributing an app, integration, or bot to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests. See Global OAuth tokens for details. The Zendesk Developer Terms prohibits you from sharing your API credentials with third parties. Client-side CORS requests are supported if the request is authenticated with an OAuth access token . The requests are not supported if the request uses a Zendesk API token. For more information and a tutorial, see Making cross-origin, browser-side API requests . Topics covered in this section: OAuth access token Global OAuth access token API token SSL requirements End user authentication For more information, see Differences between API tokens and OAuth access tokens . OAuth access token The Zendesk API supports OAuth authorization flows. For more information, see Using OAuth authentication with your application . An OAuth token gives access to a single Zendesk instance (the one with the OAuth client used to create the token). OAuth access tokens also permit client-side API requests. See Making cross-origin, browser-side API requests in the Zendesk API guide. In your requests, specify the access token in an Authorization header as follows: Authorization : Bearer { access_token } Example: Authorization : Bearer gErypPlm4dOVgGRvA1ZzMH5MQ3nLo8bo If you use curl to test different endpoints, you can use the following format: curl https://obscura.zendesk.com/api/v2/users.json \ -H "Authorization: Bearer gErypPlm4dOVgGRvA1ZzMH5MQ3nLo8bo" Access tokens can be up to 184 characters long. Global OAuth access token If you plan on making an app, integration, or bot available to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth access tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests. You may not use regular API tokens or OAuth tokens because the Zendesk Developer Terms prohibits Zendesk customers from sharing their API credentials with you. For more information, see Set up a global OAuth client . The requirement to use global OAuth tokens doesn't apply if you're developing applications or integrations for internal use. API token (deprecated) API tokens are different from OAuth tokens, which are detailed in the previous section. API tokens are auto-generated passwords in the Zendesk Admin Center. Warning: As passwords, API tokens can be used to impersonate anyone in the account, including admins. Make sure to keep them secure. Delete any unused tokens. Delete a token at once if you suspect it's been compromised and create another one if necessary. For a more secure alternative, use OAuth access tokens as described above. API tokens are managed in the Admin Center interface at Apps and integrations > APIs > Zendesk API . The page lets you view, add, or delete tokens. More than one token can be active at the same time. Deleting a token deactivates it permanently. You can have up to 256 tokens. If you're at the limit, you must delete an existing token to add a new one. Accounts that currently have more than 256 tokens have a limit of 2048 tokens. Basic authentication is used for API tokens. The credentials must be sent with the request in an Authorization header. Use the following format for the credentials: { email_address } / token : { api_token } Example: jdoe @ example . com / token : 6wiIBWbGkBMo1mRDMuVwkw1EPsNkeUj95PIz2akv After base64-encoding the resulting string, add it to the Authorization header as follows: Authorization : Basic amRvZUBleGFtcGxlLmNvbS90b2tlbjo2d2lJQldiR2tCTW8xbVJETXVWd2t3MUVQc05rZVVqOTVQSXoyYWt2 If you use curl to test different endpoints, you can use the following format: curl https://obscura.zendesk.com/api/v2/users.json \ -u [email protected] /token:6wiIBWbGkBMo1mRDMuVwkw1EPsNkeUj95PIz2akv If authenticating over HTTP, url-encode the slash character in {email_address}/token as %2F . SSL requirements The Zendesk v2 API is an SSL-only API, regardless of how your account is configured. All connections to the Zendesk API must support the TLS 1.2 protocol. Support for TLS 1.0 and 1.1 was removed in June 2018. Connections to the API must also support the SNI extension to TLS. If you connect to Zendesk through a client library, make sure it supports both TLS 1.2 and SNI. End user authentication End users can interact with the Zendesk API in two ways: anonymously or authenticated (with email and password). In open instances where users can access the help center without signing in, end users do not require authentication for any API endpoint that lists anonymous permissions. An example is the List Articles endpoint. In a closed Zendesk instance where end users must sign in to view your help center, end users can make authenticated requests to certain API endpoints, such as api/v2/requests , using their email and password if password access for end users is enabled. This allows end users to securely create, view, or update their own requests through the API. For more information on closed Zendesk instances, see Options for end-user access in Zendesk help. A setting in Admin Center lets you explicitly enable or disable password access for end users in closed instances. See Turning on and off API access . See plans & pricing Calculate your ROI Launch your first AI agent today Try for free Get a demo Need to know more? View FAQs Hide FAQs What is Zendesk? Zendesk is an AI-first service platform powered by self-learning AI agents and the Zendesk Resolution Platform . With Zendesk, organizations can resolve customer and employee requests faster and more accurately across all channels, like email, messaging, live chat, phone, social, and help center. It brings conversations, context, and workflows into one intelligent system so teams can deliver real resolutions, not just close tickets. What is Zendesk AI? Zendesk AI is the intelligence that powers the helpdesk and the broader Zendesk service platform. With Zendesk AI you can: automate common requests, help agents work faster with suggested replies and summaries, route work more accurately, and improve quality over time. Zendesk AI works best when you connect it to your real support data and keep your knowledge content up to date. Many teams start with AI assistance for agents, then expand to more automation as trust builds. What is Zendesk Resolution Platform? The Zendesk Resolution Platform is the full Zendesk service system, powered by Zendesk AI. It connects AI agents and your team members with core service tools like ticketing , helpdesk, knowledge , analytics , and quality assurance , so you can resolve issues end-to-end across all channels. Zendesk AI Agents learn from each service interaction in what we call the Resolution Learning Loop™. Each new service interaction learns from the last, making self-service better, automation more efficient, and helping your team improve speed and quality over time. What can you use Zendesk for? Run an AI-powered customer service helpdesk across all channels Zendesk allows teams to manage tickets and conversations from email, chat , phone , social, messaging apps , and help center in one interface. Teams choose Zendesk for strong ticket organization, routing, collaboration, and reminders that keep work from slipping. Manage self-service and build knowledge Create internal and external help centers and scale self-service with reusable knowledge and automation. Support employees Deliver employee service for IT , HR and shared services with structured workflows that guide requests through resolution. Operate a service-focused contact center Operate a service-focused contact center with voice and intelligent channel routing and reporting and performance insights that scale across every channel. Integrate service with the rest of your systems Integrate Zendesk with your existing systems through prebuilt integrations and APIs to reduce manual work and speed up collaboration. Does Zendesk offer standalone AI agents? Yes. Zendesk offers self-improving AI agents that can work with your existing service platform, so you can automate service without switching your help desk or service stack. Today, this capability is available through Forethought by Zendesk . How is Zendesk different from traditional customer service software? Traditional tools often stop at ticket tracking. Zendesk is built to help you resolve issues across all channels, with AI and automation built into the workflow. With Zendesk you get: One unified workspace across channels so agents manage email, chat, phone, social, and messaging in one place. Automation you can tailor to your business (routing, triggers, workflows). This is powerful for complex operations, though it can take time to learn and tune. A platform approach with knowledge, analytics, QA, and integrations working together, instead of stitching separate tools together. Self-improving AI for real resolutions Zendesk AI is designed to get better over time. The Zendesk Resolution Learning Loop uses outcomes and service signals to improve automation, quality, and agent effectiveness. Is Zendesk right for enterprises and growing businesses? Zendesk works for organizations at every stage of growth across multiple industries. From large enterprises , to startups and small teams , any business can start with a simple helpdesk setup, then scale into a full, AI-powered service operation as your needs grow. Whether you’re building our support for the first time, or growing fast and managing high volume with strict controls, Zendesk adapts to your workflow, systems, and security requirements. pages.title: Betas and EAPs | Zendesk Developer Docs
pages.text: Betas and EAPs | Zendesk Developer Docs Documentation API Reference Search / Betas and EAPs Home Betas and EAPs Betas and EAPs On this page IT asset management Help center authentication for messaging Web Widget WFM Reports API for enhancing report generation Betas and EAPs On this page IT asset management Help center authentication for messaging Web Widget WFM Reports API for enhancing report generation Copy page At Zendesk, we value the feedback of our customers and consider it an important part of our process. That's why we offer early access for some features in development, so that you can try out the feature in advance and give us feedback or report issues. We may also provide other feedback opportunities during the development process.Â For a complete list of UI-based EAPs and betas, see Current and upcoming Zendesk betas . In addition to participating in early access programs (EAPs) and betas, you might want to join our Experience Research Panel to learn about UX research opportunities where you can help shape our products. We're offering opportunities for developers to give input in the following areas: IT asset management The IT asset management (ITAM) early access program enables employee service teams to track, monitor, and manage assets directly alongside ticket workflows. By managing your IT assets in Zendesk, you can ensure agents have access to view and manage the latest asset data without having to switch tools. To participate in the ITAM EAP, turn on the feature in Admin Center and accept the terms and conditions. For more information, see IT asset management . Help center authentication for messaging Web Widget This early access program provides a seamless authentication experience for messaging users through the Web Widget within a Zendesk help center. When users are signed into the help center, their identity, including name and email, is automatically shared with bots and agents during messaging interactions. For more information, see help center authentication for messaging (EAP) . To participate in the EAP, see Help Center authentication for messaging - Early Access Program . WFM Reports API for enhancing report generation The Reports endpoint of the Workforce Management (WFM) Public API lets you extract data from both default and custom reports by specifying the id of the desired report template. You can customize grouping, filter criteria, and use several metrics when generating your reports. The Agent Activity endpoint offers data on agent activity start and end time timestamps, including the events that mark the agents' start and end days. This API is available only for Zendesk WFM customers (previously Tymeshift). Note : This API does not follow the general mechanisms and conventions of most Zendesk APIs. pages.text: Changelog | Zendesk Developer Docs Documentation API Reference Search / Changelog Home Changelog Changelog Changelog This changelog lists only significant changes, not all changes, to the Zendesk developer platform. It includes changes announced after June 22, 2022. For earlier announcements, see Developer Updates in Zendesk help. Â Filter by event type Date Event Subject Description Sep 14, 2026 Deprecated Templating API Starting September 14, 2026, Zendesk will begin a phased end-of-life process for Help Center Templating API v1, v2, and v3. To maintain your help center's functionality and styling, you must upgrade to Templating API v4 . On September 14, 2026, Zendesk will block the import of v1, v2, and v3 themes for all new Zendesk accounts. On March 1, 2027, importing v1, v2, and v3 themes will be completely blocked for all accounts. On August 3, 2027, all remaining legacy themes will be automatically upgraded to v4, and v1, v2, and v3 will be completely removed. See Upgrading from Templating API v1 , Upgrading from Templating API v2 , and Upgrading from Templating API v3 . Aug 26, 2026 Deprecated OAuth Tokens The Create Token ( /api/v2/oauth/tokens ) endpoint is deprecated. Use Create Token for Grant Type instead. July 6, 2026 Breaking change IT Asset Management Assets API Starting August 6, 2026, the purchase_cost field on assets will change from a plain number to an object with amount and currency properties. June 24, 2026 Deprecated Jira integration Zendesk will be delisting the Jira Integration V2 and re-listing the original version. Customers already on V2 should remain on V2 and will be supported by Zendesk for now. Zendesk will reach out to V2 customers with next steps. June 1, 2026 Deprecated API tokens Starting July 28, 2026, Zendesk will begin a phased end-of-life process for API tokens. On July 28, 2026, any token unused for 30 days or more will be deactivated. Deactivated tokens can't be used to make API requests. Tokens that remain deactivated for 60 days or more will be permanently deleted. Accounts created on or after July 28, 2026 won't be able to create or use API tokens. You can reactivate deactivated tokens during the 60-day grace period before they're permanently deleted. Starting October 27, 2026, accounts can no longer create new API tokens through the UI or API. Existing active tokens will remain usable until April 30, 2027 unless they are deactivated. On April 30, 2027, all remaining API tokens will be permanently deactivated. Admins will no longer be able to reactivate tokens, and the API token management pages will be removed from Admin Center. See Security and authentication for related authentication options. May 19, 2026 Deprecated AI Agents API base URL Starting July 1, 2026, the legacy *.ultimate.ai API base URL is deprecated. Use the {subdomain}.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api API base URL instead. Mar 10, 2026 Added Create Request endpoint Added an email verification workflow for anonymous requests created through the Create Request endpoint to help prevent spam. Anonymous requests now create a suspended ticket until the requester verifies their email address . See Creating anonymous requests . Feb 3, 2026 Deprecated request list helper Starting Feb 3, 2026 the beta {{request_list}} helper is deprecated. For information on customizing the request list, see the request-list part of the Copenhagen theme repository code base. Jan 30, 2026 Deprecated Show location API Starting April 30, 2026, the /api/v2/apps/locations/{app_location_id} endpoint is deprecated for all accounts. Jan 16, 2026 Breaking change OAuth access and refresh tokens Starting February 2, 2026, Zendesk is enforcing default token expiration (TTL) and requiring the refresh token flow for global (external) OAuth clients. This includes all newly created global clients and existing global clients with no usage in the past 3 months. Global clients with recent usage will have expirations applied progressively as part of our security enhancements. Starting April 30, 2026, newly created local (non-global) OAuth clients will also receive the same default TTLs automatically and the deadline to adopt the refresh token flow is April 1, 2027. See Using OAuth to authenticate Zendesk API requests in a web app . Jan 14, 2026 Breaking change Zendesk Apps framework settings Starting April 29, 2026, Zendesk apps no longer support the "password" setting in installation settings ( parameters[].type = "password" in manifest.json ). Apps that previously used a password field must migrate to OAuth where supported or store credentials using a secure setting (for example, "type": "text" with "secure": true ). See Using secure settings . December 18, 2025 Deprecated Legacy AI Agents Data Export API Beginning December 18, 2025, the legacy AI Agents Data Export API is deprecated. It will reach end of life on May 29, 2026. Instead, use AI Agents Data Export API . Sep 10, 2025 Breaking change Unity sdk Beginning with version 4.0.0 of the Unity SDK, the core SDK no longer includes support for Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Japanese, Korean, and Thai. To use these languages in your Unity project, you'll need to install the appropriate font packages separately. Sep 9, 2025 Deprecated Zendesk Sell Starting August 31, 2027, Zendesk Sell will be retired. You will continue to have full access to the product until that date. Aug 28, 2025 Deprecated Sunshine Conversations wrappers Starting August 28, 2025, Zendesk will no longer update or maintain the Python , Ruby , Java , and JavaScript SDK libraries for the Sunshine Conversations API. See Sunshine Conversations API specification . July 7, 2025 Breaking change Legacy custom objects Starting January 15, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new legacy custom objects or relationships. Zendesk will fully remove legacy custom objects in July 2026. Your existing legacy custom objects and records will remain accessible until that time. See Migrating legacy custom objects to the new custom objects experience . Jun 27, 2025 Breaking change Incremental User Export Starting June 27, 2025, rate limits will apply to Incremental User Export cursor-based operations. Standard accounts will be limited to 20 requests per minute, while accounts with the high-volume API add-on will have a limit of 60 requests per minute. See Incremental User Export, Cursor Based May 15, 2025 Breaking change Tickets API Beginning May 15, 2025, all ticket updates will be protected by a concurrency control mechanism called optimistic locking. Any collisions that occur on unprotected endpoints will now return a 409 Conflict value instead of the previously inaccurate 200 OK value. See Protecting against ticket update collisions April 25, 2025 Breaking change Omnichannel routing engagements When filtering a list of engagements, start_time and end_time values must be specified in Unix epoch time in seconds. Previously these values were in milliseconds. For example, 1630000000 corresponds to a specific date and time (e.g., 2021-08-26T17:46:40Z UTC). See Listing engagements . April 23, 2025 Deprecated Chat Web SDK Beginning April 30, Zendesk will no longer support new integrations using Chat Conversation APIs and the Chat WebSDK . Existing integrations will continue to work, but customers are encouraged to switch to Zendesk Messaging . If youâre using Zendesk Chat and want to add a bot, use Zendesk AI Agents . For third-party bot integrations, use Zendesk Messaging and the Sunshine Conversations APIs . April 3, 2025 Added User Identities Introduced the verification_method and verified_at properties to indicate whether a user has verified their email address, the method of verification, and the date it was verified. January 21, 2025 Breaking change Account Settings Beginning February 24, 2025, the cdn property in the Account Show Settings endpoint will show the current default and secondary (fallback) CDN URLs used by the Support agent interface. December 9, 2024 Added Omnichannel Routing Queues Introducing APIs to create and manage custom queues for omnichannel routing. See Understanding how omnichannel routing uses queues to route work to agents and Omnichannel Routing Queues . Oct 31, 2024 Breaking change ZIS Bundles Beginning December 5, 2025, ZIS bundles can no longer be uploaded or updated if they contain an OAuth access token reference path. Instead, use the connectionName property to refer to the connection in your custom action definitions. See Using a connection to authenticate API requests in a ZIS flow . October 28, 2024 Removed Targets Support for all URL and brand-specific targets has ended. If you need to notify a URL or an external service, use webhooks . External email targets are still supported. Oct 21, 2024 Added Redirect Rules Redirect Rules API is now GA. This API enables the creation and management of redirects for deleted or archived content like articles and posts, preventing users from encountering 404 errors on outdated links. Sep 12, 2024 Breaking change Offered to event Added a new offered to event when omnichannel routing offers a ticket to an agent. This new event replaces the previously used Change type event with field name = 'offered to' to log an offer by omnichannel routing. Aug 29, 2024 Added Reorder ticket fields Added the /api/v2/ticket_fields/reorder.json endpoint, allowing you to set the display order of ticket fields. See Reorder Ticket Fields . Aug 27, 2024 Deprecated Less secure OAuth grant types Beginning February 17, 2025, the implicit and password grant flows can no longer be used to get OAuth access tokens. If you're using OAuth 2.0 to authenticate API requests, you must switch to the authorization code grant flow . See also Using PKCE to make Zendesk OAuth access tokens more secure . Aug 19, 2024 Deprecated Zopim Chat REST API Beginning May 12, 2025, Live Chat API endpoints that use the www.zopim.com/api/v2 path will stop working. We recommend migrating to {subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/chat endpoints as soon as possible. See the Live Chat reference . Aug 12, 2024 Deprecated Zendesk Events Connector for Amazon EventBridge Starting August 12, 2024, the Events Connector for Amazon EventBridge can't be used to create new event connections. Existing event connections will continue working until December 1, 2025. We recommend migrating all events to webhooks prior to that date. See Using webhooks to integrate with Amazon EventBridge . Aug 2, 2024 Breaking change Skill-based routing Starting September 2, 2024, the Incremental Instance Values Export endpoint will sort based on the updated_at timestamp instead of the created_at timestamp of instance values. As a result, associate events will advance to align with unassociate events, whereas previously, unassociate events were retroactively aligned with associate events. Jul 2, 2024 Added Help Center templating API Introduced Help Center Templating API v4 and an update to the Copenhagen theme. See Upgrading from Templating API v3 . Jul 1, 2024 Deprecated Basic authentication Starting July 31, 2024, basic authentication using an email and password is deprecated for /api/v2/ endpoints for new accounts and for accounts that are not using this method. If youâre actively using this method today, you will be able to continue using it until January 12, 2026. Jul 1, 2024 Deprecated Chat Conversations APIs Starting July 1, 2024, Chat Conversations APIs are deprecated for new accounts and for accounts not using these APIs. If you're actively using these APIs today, you will be able to continue using them. Jun 10, 2024 Added Account Groups Availability API Introduced the ability to view aggregated status, workload, and capacity data for groups of agents. See Get Account Groups Availability . Apr 2, 2024 Breaking change Article Attachments API Article attachment responses no longer include the attachment file name in the URL after content_url . You can continue to use the body's file_name property for the file name. See Announcing a URL structure update for the Article Attachments API . Apr 1, 2024 New EAP WFM Public API Agent Activity endpoint Introduced a new endpoint for the WFM Public API that lets you extract data for agents' activities based on start and end time. This includes start and end day events. Note : This API is available only for Zendesk WFM customers (previously Tymeshift). Feb 21, 2024 Added Zendesk SDK for Unity Zendesk SDK for Unity has exited the Early Access Program and is now available for everyone. See Working with messaging for your mobile channel in Zendesk help for configuring Unity as a channel in the Admin Center. Feb 1, 2024 New EAP WFM Public API Reports endpoint Introduced the ability to extract data from both default and custom reports by specifying the ID of the desired report template. Note : This API is available only for Zendesk WFM customers (previously Tymeshift). Jan 8, 2024 Added OAS files Made the OpenAPI specifications for the Ticketing and Help Center APIs available as OAS file downloads. You can download them from the Ticketing and Help Center home pages. Oct 12, 2023 Breaking change JWT Changed the https://yoursubdomain.zendesk.com/access/jwt endpoint method from GET to POST. See How JWT SSO for Zendesk works in Zendesk help for how this URL is used in the SSO workflow. October 4, 2023 Added Access Logs API Introduced the ability to capture the data an agent or admin has accessed in your Zendesk account within the last 90 days. You can use the access logs to identify data security risks, refine security and privacy policies, and support data privacy compliance. The Access Logs API consists of the following endpoint: List Access Logs See Monitoring agent activity with the Access Log API in Zendesk help. September 26, 2023 Added Custom objects API Introduced the ability to create custom objects to capture data that doesn't fit into standard objects such as tickets, users, or organizations. The Custom Objects API includes the following endpoint collections: Custom Objects Custom Object Fields Custom Object Records See Getting started with custom objects . July 11, 2023 New EAP Redirect rules for help center URLs Introduced the ability to create and manage 301 and 302 redirect rules for help center URLs that would otherwise return 404 page not found errors. July 6, 2023 Added Messaging Metadata Ability to send metadata from a messaging conversation through the Zendesk Web Widget, Zendesk SDKs for Android or iOS, or Zendesk SDK for Unity See Using Messaging Metadata with the Zendesk Web Widget and SDKs . July 3, 2023 Added Help Center JWT Introduced the ability to include a JSON Web Token (JWT) when making client-side requests to third-part APIs from a help center. Added two new APIs: New Token List Public Keys See Making third-party API requests with help center JWTs . June 12, 2023 Added Macros API Added the ability for admins to view personal macros created by and available only to individual users. See List Macros . May 22, 2023 Breaking change Offset-based pagination Offset-based pagination requests after the first 10,000 records will return an error message. See New limits for offset-based pagination . May 19, 2023 Removed Merge Self With Another User The Merge Self with Another User endpoint is being removed and replaced with the Merge End Users endpoint. Apr 30, 2023 Removed NPSÂ® API Removed the Net Promoter Scoreâ (NPSÂ®) API. See Announcing the removal of Net Promoter Score (NPS) . Apr 25, 2023 Added Agent Availability APIs Introduced the ability to access and update real-time agent status and activity information across Zendesk channels. Added two new APIs: Agent Availability API Unified Agent Status API Previously, these APIs were only available as part of the Agent Availability API EAP . For more information, see Agent Availability APIs . Apr 17, 2023 Added ZIS LoadLinks action Added cursor pagination to the ZIS LoadLinks action. The action now supports the page_size , page_after_cursor , and page_before_cursor parameters. Responses from the LoadLinks action now include a meta object property that contains pagination information. For more information, see cursor pagination in the ZIS Links documentation. Apr 12, 2023 New EAP New Custom Objects API Introduced the ability to create custom objects to capture data that doesn't fit into standard objects such as tickets, users, or organizations. The Custom Objects API includes the following endpoint collections: Custom Objects Custom Object Fields Custom Object Records See Custom Objects EAP and Custom Objects API . Mar 30, 2023 Added Webhooks API Added a new custom_headers property to webhooks and the authentication property now supports api_key as a type. See Creating and monitoring webhooks . Mar 2, 2023 Deprecated Status API Four Status API endpoints are being deprecated. Three new endpoints replaces them. To be removed: List components Show component status List subcomponents Show subcomponent status Added: List active incidents List maintenance incidents Show active incident See Announcing the deprecation and replacement of Status API endpoints . Jan 17, 2023 Deprecated NPSÂ® API The Net Promoter Scoreâ (NPSÂ®) API is being deprecated. See Announcing the removal of Net Promoter Score (NPS) . Jan 17, 2023 Added Custom Ticket Statuses API Introduced the ability to create and manage more granular and customized ticket statuses. See Announcing custom ticket statuses and Custom ticket statuses API . Oct 7, 2022 Breaking change Voice API Updated two Voice endpoints to support omnichannel routing and unified agent status: Show availability Update availability See Voice Availabilities . Sep 20, 2022 New EAP Custom Ticket Statuses API Introduced the ability to create and manage more granular and customized ticket statuses. See Announcing the Custom Ticket Statuses EAP and Custom ticket statuses API . Jun 29, 2022 Removed Support Users API Removed the end user endpoints. See Announcing the removal of end user API endpoints in Support . Jun 22, 2022 New EAP Messaging in the Unity SDK Introduced two new methods for messaging in the Unity SDK: ZendeskMessaging.Initialize() ZendeskMessaging.Instance.ShowMessaging() See Getting started .
